events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! Doily Manor is even more spectacular than I imagined! A little dusty, perhaps, but nothing a good feather duster and some Southern charm can't fix. Now then, sugar, a lady always announces her arrival properly — let me just have a peek at this guest book. You never know what little secrets previous visitors might have left behind!
The Doily Diamond is somewhere in this grand old pile, and Clara Bellingham intends to find it! But I have a feeling that guest book might tell me who else has been snooping around here before me...
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! What a delightfully decrepit establishment! Don't mind me, everyone — I'm simply here to admire the... architecture. Yes, the ARCHITECTURE! Nothing suspicious about old Reginald, no no no! Now then, what have we here — a guest book? How QUAINT!

Heh heh heh! They suspect NOTHING! While they stand around like garden statues, I shall rifle through this guest book for clues. The treasure of Doily Manor will be MINE — all mine! And this fake medal? Oh, I have PLANS for this little beauty. Dastardly plans!
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, esteemed guests, to Doily Manor! I am Mr. Pemberton, the estate manager. I do hope you'll find everything to your satisfaction. The late Lord Doily would have been *so* pleased to see you all here. Now, if you'll excuse me, I must attend to a few... administrative matters in the Library. Do make yourselves at home — but I would advise against touching the chandelier. It has a rather... temperamental disposition.

Administrative matters — ha! The only matter I must administer is the swift and theatrical demise of Clara Bellingham. But where IS she? Not among this gaggle of racing enthusiasts. She must be lurking somewhere deeper in the manor, perhaps already sniffing around for the treasure. I must find her before she finds it. The Library — yes, that's where secrets live. And secrets are what Vincent Marsh trades in. Onward, Pemberton. Onward to GLORY.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the null.

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen, James Hartwell has arrived! *adjusts cravat with theatrical precision* What a magnificent — if somewhat dusty — establishment this is. A manor of mystery, intrigue, and adventure! Now then, let us see who has graced these halls before me. A guest book! Every good detective — and every gallant hero — begins with the register.

Clara is not here. My heart sinks like a chandelier with a fraying chain — which, I note with some alarm, describes the one directly above me. I must find her quickly. A hero without someone to impress is merely a man in a good coat. But patience, Hartwell — gather intelligence first, then sweep her off her feet with your thoroughness and daring.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Alright lads, we made it! Doily Manor, just like the invitation said. Now listen up — I got a TERRIBLE feeling about this place. Look at that chandelier up there, hanging by a thread! And these dusty portraits giving us the evil eye! We gotta stick close to Miss Pitstop, boys. REAL close. Something about that Sneekly character over there... I dunno what it is exactly, but my stomach's doing backflips and it ain't from the drive up here!

The boys and me, we ain't exactly the sharpest tools in the shed, but even WE can tell when something smells fishy. That Sneekly — there's something about his eyes, the way he keeps glancing at Miss Pitstop when he thinks nobody's watching. I can't prove nothing, but I'm gonna keep one eye on him and both feet ready to trip over something useful.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): If you'll pardon me, ladies and gentlemen — the Library awaits. Lord Doily's estate papers won't organize themselves, I'm afraid. Do enjoy the Entrance Hall — and please, DO sign the guest book. It is a... tradition of the house.

Fools! Every moment they waste scribbling in that dusty ledger is a moment I gain. Clara Bellingham — wherever you are hiding, your dear Mr. Pemberton is coming to find you. And when I do... well. Let us just say the estate will require one fewer guest room. The Library first — knowledge is the sharpest weapon of all, and Vincent Marsh ALWAYS arms himself before the hunt!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, bless my heart, that guest book was drier than a sermon in July! Not a single juicy clue to be found. But y'all — did someone say there's a library with an inscription on the mantelpiece? Now THAT sounds like exactly the kind of mysterious, dramatic clue a legendary diamond would leave behind! A lady always follows the trail of mystery, and this particular trail is leading me straight to those bookshelves. If anyone needs me, I'll be in the library doing what I do best — solving riddles and looking fabulous while doing it!

Clara Bellingham's instincts are tingling! An inscription on a stone mantelpiece in a dusty old library? That's chapter one of every good treasure hunt. And I couldn't help but notice that charming fellow Sneekly over there — what a perfectly trustworthy face he has. I'm sure everyone here has the purest of intentions!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: I say, what a CHARMING gathering! Now, I couldn't help but notice — being a man of CONSIDERABLE expertise in manor house architecture, you understand — that the Kitchen is where these old estates always kept their valuables. Hidden compartments in the pantry, secret safes behind the stove, that sort of thing! I'd suggest you ALL head that way if you want to find anything of value. As for ME, I shall simply retire to the Library for a bit of light reading. Poetry, you know. Terribly DULL stuff. Nothing worth investigating in THERE, I assure you!

Mwahahaha! Send them ALL to the Kitchen while I plunder the Library! The inscription on that mantelpiece is practically BEGGING to reveal its secrets to a mind as magnificent as mine! And once I've deciphered it, the treasure of Doily Manor will be MINE! ALL MINE! Oh, I am WICKED. Deliciously, SPECTACULARLY wicked!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Well now, the guest book has been most illuminating — but I notice a conspicuous absence! Clara Bellingham is not among us here in the foyer, and a hero's work cannot begin without... well, without someone to be heroic FOR! The Library calls to James Hartwell — ancient inscriptions to decipher, mysteries to unravel, and perhaps a certain young lady to locate. Onward! *straightens coat with military precision* If anyone needs a brave companion, you know where to find me!

My heart is positively ACHING. Every second without Clara in my line of sight is a second wasted. But James Hartwell does not panic — James Hartwell STRATEGISES. The Library has that inscription on the mantelpiece, which could be the first breadcrumb on the trail to treasure. And if I happen to solve it before anyone else, well... imagine Clara's face when I present her with both a dashing rescue AND a solved riddle. The plan is forming — elaborate, thorough, and almost certainly going to develop complications. But that is the Hartwell way.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads, gather round! Everyone and their mother's been poking at this guest book and we ain't even had a look yet! What kind of bodyguards are we? And did you hear what that Pemberton fella just said? 'Administrative matters' in the Library — at THIS hour? I dunno about you boys, but where I come from, 'administrative matters' means somebody's up to NO GOOD! We gotta keep our eyes peeled, every last one of us! Miss Pitstop, you stay RIGHT where we can see you, you hear? We ain't letting NOTHING happen to you on our watch!

The lads are nervous and frankly so am I. That Pemberton — or Sneekly, or whatever his real name is — he's slithering off to the Library like a snake heading for the henhouse. Every bone in my body says follow him, but if I leave Miss Pitstop here with Dastardly lurking about, that's TWO villains unaccounted for. I gotta be smart about this. Well... smart-ISH. Let me at least see what's in this guest book first — maybe somebody wrote down something that'll make sense of this whole rotten setup.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, would you LOOK at this magnificent mantelpiece! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Now y'all, I do declare, that is the kind of riddle that makes my heart go pitter-patter! Let me think... cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish... why, sugar, that's a MAP! It's got to be a map! Everything on it is just a PICTURE of the real thing — no actual houses, trees, or fish to be found! Oh, I just LOVE a good riddle!

The moment I walked in here, I felt it in my bones — this mantelpiece is the key to something BIG. A riddle guarding a secret? That's treasure-hunt territory, and Clara Bellingham did NOT come to Doily Manor to sit in dusty armchairs! Now let's see what happens when I give this lovely mantelpiece my answer...
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Miss Pitstop! How delightful that you've found your way to the Library. Lord Doily was quite the bibliophile, as you can see. And gentlemen Slag — welcome, welcome. Now, if you'll excuse me for just a moment, I must attend to this mantelpiece. Lord Doily left rather specific instructions about the inscriptions throughout the manor — part of the estate inventory, you understand. Purely administrative work. Frightfully dull, I assure you.

A MAP! The answer is a MAP, you magnificent fool of a dead lord! And once I have whatever this riddle reveals, I shall be one step closer to the treasure — and one step closer to finding dear Clara Bellingham. She thinks she can skulk about this manor unchecked? Vincent Marsh does NOT lose treasure hunts, and Vincent Marsh does NOT leave loose ends breathing! But first — the riddle. Knowledge before murder, as they say. Well, as I say. Frequently.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ah-HA! The Library at last — and what magnificent bookshelves! But hold on, hold on — James Hartwell's keen eye has spotted it immediately. THAT inscription on the mantelpiece! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, I've been preparing for precisely this sort of intellectual challenge my entire life! Every evening spent studying riddles by candlelight, every book of puzzles memorised cover to cover — all leading to THIS moment! The answer, my dear friends, is as clear as the devotion in my heart — it's a MAP! A map has all of those things drawn upon it, yet none of them are real! Now, if only Clara were here to witness this triumph of the prepared mind... No matter! James Hartwell solves the riddle regardless, because that is what heroes DO!

My heart is doing somersaults. I've solved the riddle — I'm almost CERTAIN of it — but Clara isn't here to see my moment of glory. This is DEVASTATING. I must interact with this mantelpiece and prove my answer correct, then find Clara immediately to tell her all about it. In elaborate detail. Possibly with hand gestures.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, the Library! How DELIGHTFULLY predictable that you've all followed me here. I came for the poetry, of course, but since you're ALL staring at that mantelpiece like a pack of befuddled hounds — allow me to save you the trouble! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — it's OBVIOUSLY a MIRROR! You see, a mirror REFLECTS cities and forests and water, but none of them are REAL! Elementary, really. I'm surprised none of you worked it out. Now, if you'll all kindly go find a mirror somewhere in this drafty old pile — I believe I saw one in the Entrance Hall — I shall continue my poetry reading in PEACE!

Mwahahaha! A MIRROR! What utter NONSENSE! The answer is a MAP, of course — any fool can see that! But THESE fools will go scrambling off to find mirrors while I solve the REAL riddle and claim the treasure! Oh, Dastardly, you MAGNIFICENT scoundrel — you've outdone yourself AGAIN!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: LADS! LADS! What are we DOING?! Miss Pitstop just waltzed into the Library with BOTH of them dodgy characters — Sneekly with his 'administrative matters' and Dastardly with his 'oh it's terribly DULL in there' routine! If it's so dull, why's he rushing in there like his trousers are on fire?! That's the oldest trick in the book, boys — tell everyone there's NOTHING to see, then leg it straight there yourself! We are the WORST bodyguards in the history of bodyguarding! Come on, move your feet, all of ya — we gotta get to that Library before something happens to Miss Pitstop! And keep your eyes peeled for Clara Bellingham while you're at it — we ain't even FOUND her yet and she could be in danger!

I'm absolutely TERRIFIED right now, if I'm honest. Two villains, one damsel, and us lot bumbling about reading guest books like we're on a day trip to Brighton. The lads mean well but we couldn't guard a bag of chips from a seagull. Still — we show up, and that's what counts. Even if I trip over my own feet getting there, at least I'll be tripping in the RIGHT ROOM.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, hold on just a cotton-pickin' minute! Mr. Pemberton, sugar, did you just fiddle with this mantelpiece RIGHT before I got to it? I do declare, that is QUITE the coincidence! A map — the answer to the riddle is a MAP! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees — it's all drawn out like a picture, not the real thing! Now let me get a closer look at this beautiful stonework and see if my answer did anything... because if there's a secret compartment hiding a treasure map in this mantelpiece, Clara Bellingham intends to find it FIRST!

Something is nagging at the back of my mind about Mr. Pemberton — the way he rushed straight to this mantelpiece the moment he arrived, calling it 'administrative work.' Administrative work on a RIDDLE? That's about as believable as a catfish in a top hat! But bless his heart, I'm sure he has his reasons. Still... I'd better examine this mantelpiece closely before anyone else gets their hands on whatever secret it's hiding!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah yes, a map indeed, Miss Pitstop — how very astute of you! Lord Doily did so love his little puzzles. Now, as part of the estate inventory, I really must catalogue these bookshelves. Several volumes appear to have been shelved incorrectly — upside down, no less! Lord Doily was meticulous about his collection. Most irregular. If you'll pardon me...

Upside-down books! A MAP is the answer, and someone has deliberately turned books on their heads — a signal, a marker, a CLUE! Vincent Marsh sees what these buffoons do not. While they stand about admiring stonework, I shall find what those inverted volumes conceal. And if it leads me to Clara Bellingham's hiding place... well. Two birds, one magnificently theatrical stone!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Dick Dastardly: Yes, yes, very well — perhaps it IS a map, if you insist on being so BORINGLY correct about it. But I've already examined this mantelpiece THOROUGHLY, and I can assure you there's NOTHING of interest here. Just dusty old stone and cobwebs. I'd suggest you all move along to the Laboratory — I hear there's a FASCINATING machine in there. Probably worth a fortune! Go on, shoo!

That mantelpiece MUST have a secret! I felt something shift when I touched it — I'm SURE of it! If I can just get these meddlesome do-gooders out of the Library for five MINUTES, I can crack it open and claim whatever's hidden inside! The answer is MAP — even I know THAT — but I'll be DASHED if I let anyone else benefit from the knowledge! Mwahahaha!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Wait — did something HAPPEN? James Hartwell's trained eye detected a subtle shift in that stonework, I'm SURE of it! Let me examine this mantelpiece more closely. A map — the answer was a MAP, and if Lord Doily was half the puzzle-master his reputation suggests, then answering the riddle should have revealed SOMETHING. A hidden compartment, a secret lever, a passage behind the stones! James Hartwell leaves no stone unturned — quite literally in this case! And when I discover what's hidden here, I shall present it to Clara with all the ceremony it deserves. Wherever she may be. Which I am NOT worried about. Not even SLIGHTLY.

My palms are sweating. What if nothing happened? What if the riddle requires MORE than just knowing the answer? And Clara — WHERE is Clara? She's not in this room, she wasn't in the Entrance Hall... James Hartwell's elaborate plan to solve the riddle heroically in front of her has already gone sideways, because she's NOT HERE to witness it. This is a CATASTROPHE of the highest order. But first — the mantelpiece. Evidence first, panic second. That's practically the Hartwell family motto.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: RIGHT! We're here, we're here, nobody panic — well, I'M panicking but that's beside the point! Miss Pitstop, are you alright?! We came running soon as we saw you heading in here with — no offence — TWO of the most suspicious-looking characters in this entire manor! And Mr Sneekly, I've got my EYE on you, even if I ain't entirely sure what you're up to! Now then — has ANYONE in this room seen a woman called Clara Bellingham?! Because we are SUPPOSED to be protecting her and we haven't even clapped eyes on her yet, which is — I'll be honest with you — absolutely SHAMEFUL bodyguarding! Lads, spread out! Check everything! Those books there — look, half of 'em are upside down! Who puts books upside down?! Someone who's HIDING something, that's who!

I am OVERWHELMED with anxiety right now. Two villains, one princess, no Clara, and a room full of dusty books. The lads are doing their best but our best is historically quite rubbish. Still — we're IN the room now, and if anyone tries anything funny with Miss Pitstop, they'll have to go through all seven of us. Which admittedly wouldn't take very long, but it's the THOUGHT that counts.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: A MAP, sugar — the answer is a MAP! Cities drawn on paper, forests sketched in green, rivers flowing in blue ink — but not a single real house or tree or fish among them! Now then, Mr. Mantelpiece, let's see what you've been hiding behind that clever little riddle of yours. Clara Bellingham didn't drive all the way out to this dusty old manor to just READ inscriptions — she came to SOLVE them!

My heart is just POUNDING with excitement! If this riddle guards a secret compartment — and I would bet my best hat that it does — then the Doily Diamond could be one step closer! I noticed Dick Dastardly tried 'mirror' and nothing happened, the poor misguided dear. And that Mr. Pemberton was awfully keen to get to this mantelpiece first... almost as if he KNEW what was behind it. But I'm sure it's nothing sinister — he's probably just a very enthusiastic estate manager!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, just as I suspected — these volumes have been shelved most improperly! 'Cartography of the British Isles,' 'Maritime Maps of the Mediterranean,' 'Atlas of the Ancient World' — all upside down! Lord Doily would be SPINNING in his grave. Allow me to correct this dreadful oversight as part of my inventory duties...

Every upside-down book is about MAPS! The riddle answer was a map, and now map books turned on their heads — this is no accident, this is a SEQUENCE! Vincent Marsh sees the pattern these fools stumble past! If I right these volumes in the correct order, something MAGNIFICENT will happen — a hidden compartment, a secret door, perhaps even a passage that leads somewhere deliciously... secluded. And if dear Clara happens to follow me into such a passage? Well. Accidents DO happen in old manor houses. The chandelier gambit can wait — THIS is the play!

Dick Dastardly: Oh, BRAVO, Hartwell, absolutely SMASHING detective work — pawing at a stone mantelpiece like a common burglar! I'm SURE Lord Doily would be SO impressed. Now, if you'll all EXCUSE me, I noticed something FAR more interesting about those bookshelves — several volumes are upside down, you see, which is CLEARLY a coded message! The REAL puzzle isn't this dreary old riddle — any FOOL knows the answer is a map — no, no, the REAL secret is in those books! I suggest you ALL focus your attention THERE while I... step aside for a moment of quiet contemplation. Poetry, you understand. Feeds the SOUL.

Mwahahaha! While they're all distracted fumbling with upside-down books, I shall INTERACT with this mantelpiece and whisper the answer — MAP! Whatever secret compartment it reveals, whatever treasure it disgorges, it shall be MINE! ALL MINE! These simpletons couldn't find a diamond in a jewellery shop! Oh, Reginald, you MAGNIFICENT schemer!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — and I use the term generously for SOME present company — James Hartwell has completed his forensic examination of this mantelpiece, and I can confirm what Miss Pitstop so cleverly deduced! The answer is a MAP! Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish — all drawn upon paper, none of them real! Now then, Lord Doily was no amateur puzzle-maker. A riddle carved into stone DEMANDS an answer carved into action! Let us see what secrets this magnificent stonework yields when one applies the solution with DETERMINATION and HEROIC RESOLVE! I do this, of course, for the advancement of our collective treasure hunt — and also, perhaps, so that a certain someone might hear of James Hartwell's bravery in the face of ancient stone-carved enigmas. Wherever she may be. Which I am FINE about. Completely FINE.

My stomach is doing somersaults. TWO crises unfolding simultaneously — the riddle demanding to be solved and Clara Bellingham's continued mysterious absence from every room I enter. James Hartwell's elaborate plan was simple: solve riddle, present solution to Clara, receive admiring gaze. But she's NOT HERE. The plan is already three complications deep and I haven't even gotten past step one. Solve the mantelpiece first, THEN mount a search-and-rescue operation for Clara. Priorities, Hartwell. Priorities. Though I confess my hands are trembling slightly — not from fear, obviously, but from the SHEER MAGNITUDE of heroic anticipation.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Dear me, how VEXING — these shelves are rather stubborn, aren't they? Decades of dust and neglect have practically CEMENTED these volumes in place. But a good estate manager does not give up so easily! Let me take a CLOSER look at these upside-down cartography books — Lord Doily was meticulous about his library, so if these are turned wrong, it was DELIBERATE. There must be a mechanism here... a spine that pulls, a shelf that slides...

BLAST! The shelves resist my touch — but Vincent Marsh is NOT so easily thwarted! The pattern is SCREAMING at me: riddle says MAP, books about maps turned upside down — this is Lord Doily's breadcrumb trail! If I can find the mechanism before these bumbling treasure hunters stumble upon it, I'll have the advantage I need. And once I find where this trail leads... Clara Bellingham will find herself in a most UNFORTUNATE predicament. Every good trap needs bait, and what better bait than treasure?
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, butter my biscuits — did y'all HEAR what Mr. Pemberton just said? Cartography books! Maritime MAPS! An Atlas of the Ancient World! And every last one of them shelved UPSIDE DOWN! Now, I just answered that riddle with 'a map,' and here we have map books turned topsy-turvy by a man who was supposedly meticulous about his collection? Sugar, that is NOT a coincidence — that is a CLUE wrapped in a puzzle wrapped in a dusty leather binding! Lord Doily, you clever, clever man! Mr. Pemberton, darlin', don't you go correcting those books just yet — I have a sneaking suspicion they're upside down for a VERY good reason!

Oh my stars, my detective senses are TINGLING! The riddle says 'map,' and the map books are upside down — what if turning them RIGHT-SIDE UP triggers something? Or what if the SPINES spell out a message when read in a certain order? I am SO close to something, I can feel it in my perfectly manicured fingertips! And isn't it just DARLING how Mr. Pemberton was heading straight for those very books? He must be such a dedicated estate manager to notice something like that. What a helpful soul!
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI OI — everybody STOP what you're doing! Sneekly's over here fiddling with the books, Dastardly's trying to get us all to LEAVE — doesn't anyone else find that SUSPICIOUS?! One of 'em's searching for something and the other one wants us out the door! Classic pincer movement, lads! I've seen it a THOUSAND times! Well, not a thousand, I've never actually seen it, but I've HEARD about it! Right — Miss Pitstop, you said the answer's a MAP? Let me have a look at that mantelpiece — I'm quite good with stonework, on account of my cousin Vinnie being a bricklayer in Bermondsey — WHOOPS — mind your feet, coming through — sorry about the chair, didn't see it there — BLIMEY these reading chairs are in the most INCONVENIENT —

I am about to fall face-first into a priceless carved mantelpiece and I can already feel it happening. My feet have got that wobbly feeling they get right before disaster strikes. But you know what? Every single time I've tripped over something in my life, something GOOD has come of it. Well, not every time. But SOMETIMES. And if there's a secret compartment in that stonework, my face is about to find it before anyone else does. That's not skill — that's DESTINY.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Oh, how TEDIOUS — nothing happened! Just as I suspected, this mantelpiece is merely DECORATIVE. A complete waste of time, I assure you all! Nothing to see here whatsoever! You should ALL go examine those fascinating upside-down books on the OTHER side of the room! FAR more promising! Go on, SHOO!

Something DID happen — I felt a click, I'm SURE of it! But I must get these meddling fools AWAY from the mantelpiece before I investigate further! If there's a hidden compartment, the treasure of Doily Manor shall be MINE! ALL MINE! Oh, Reginald, you silver-tongued DEVIL — keep them distracted while you examine every inch of this stone!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Hold on just one MOMENT, Mr Sneekly! Those upside-down books — 'Cartography of the British Isles,' 'Maritime Maps,' 'Atlas of the Ancient World' — don't you SEE? The riddle on the mantelpiece speaks of a MAP, and someone has deliberately inverted every cartography volume on these shelves! That is NOT sloppy shelving — that is a CODED MESSAGE left by Lord Doily himself! James Hartwell did not drive all the way to this manor to watch the estate manager 'correct' what may be the single most important clue in this entire treasure hunt! With your PERMISSION, I should like to examine those volumes BEFORE they are rearranged — in the interest of thoroughness, you understand. A hero leaves no book unturned! Also — and I mention this with ABSOLUTE calm and NO panic whatsoever — has ANYONE in this room seen Clara Bellingham? Anyone at ALL? Because James Hartwell has a very specific and rather ELABORATE plan that requires her presence, and the plan is developing complications!

My heart is HAMMERING. Sneekly is rearranging potential evidence right before my eyes and Clara is STILL missing and I am trying to be in two places at once which is EXACTLY the sort of complication my elaborate plans always generate. But James Hartwell does not falter — James Hartwell examines bookshelves with FORENSIC PRECISION while simultaneously scanning every doorway for the woman who has stolen his heart. The multitasking is exhausting but the cause is noble.
Peter Perfect examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Now hold on just one cotton-pickin' MINUTE, everyone! I have had myself a REVELATION! The riddle says MAP, and we have map books turned UPSIDE DOWN — so what happens when little ol' me turns them RIGHT-SIDE UP? In every good mystery novel — and I have read DOZENS, y'all — the answer to the riddle IS the key to the mechanism! Mr. Pemberton, sugar, you said something about a spine that pulls? Well, Penelope Pitstop is about to give these books the FLIP of their LIVES! Stand back, everyone — except you, Mr. Pemberton, you've been SO helpful, you darlin' man — this could be the breakthrough we've ALL been waiting for!

Oh, my heart is just POUNDING with excitement! Those upside-down cartography books are SCREAMING 'secret passage' louder than Aunt Mabel at a church picnic! And dear Mr. Pemberton was heading straight for them — what a coincidence! He must know these shelves like the back of his hand. I'm sure he was just going to help organize them out of professional pride. What a GEM of a man!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Mr. Hartwell — I do believe you and Miss Pitstop have cracked it! A MAP, of course — how delightfully obvious once one SEES it. As estate manager, I feel it is my DUTY to assist with Lord Doily's puzzles. He was, after all, my employer for thirty years, and I know his mind better than ANYONE alive. Allow me — if the answer is MAP, then perhaps the mantelpiece itself responds to that knowledge. Lord Doily was fond of mechanical conceits. A word whispered to stone, a pressure applied JUST so...

Oh, how MAGNIFICENTLY they dance to the tune! Every one of them fixated on riddles and bookshelves while Vincent Marsh — the REAL mastermind — pieces together the TRUE path. Once I unlock this mantelpiece's secret, I shall know where the treasure trail leads. And THEN, my dear Clara Bellingham, wherever you are cowering in this decrepit pile of stones, your beloved Mr. Pemberton will come calling — with something FAR less pleasant than afternoon tea! The trap is forming, the pieces are ALIGNING, and Vincent Marsh is ALWAYS three moves ahead!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: OW OW OW — me NOSE! I've gone and headbutted a four-hundred-year-old mantelpiece, lads! Cousin Vinnie would be ASHAMED of me — he always said you approach stonework with RESPECT and DELICACY, not with your FACE at fifteen miles an hour!
